searched: grep for other callers of get_content_by_priority/get_content_since/get_flagged_items/search_content across daemon/ to check for signature-break risk

findings.summary: The 3-4 line fragment that builds the kind filter's SQL (`placeholders = ",".join(["?"] * len(kind_filter)); query += f" AND json_extract(c.analysis, '$.kind') IN ({placeholders})"; params.extend(kind_filter)`) is written out fresh, with no shared helper, in four separate places this diff adds: `get_content_by_priority` (job-1.diff:264-267), `get_content_since` (job-1.diff:293-296), `get_flagged_items` (job-1.diff:341-344), and inline inside `search_content`'s candidate-query builder (job-1.diff:408-413, spelled slightly differently against `candidate_query`/`knn_params` instead of `query`/`params`). None of these four existed before this job; all four are new copies of the same logic added in this one diff, which is the exact shape the review guardrails call out as a finding regardless of test-pass or size. It doesn't break any criterion and the codebase already tolerates the analogous pattern for `source_filter` (also duplicated inline across the same methods, pre-existing), so this new duplication follows established file convention rather than introducing a new abstraction, and the project's own duplication gate (which ran clean per journal.jsonl's final `verified` record for job 1) apparently sits below this fragment's size. A single private helper (e.g. `_kind_filter_sql(kind_filter, params) -> str`) called from all four sites would have removed the repetition the review guardrail names as worth flagging even when it is small and passes every test as-is.
